mainTopic: רבי יהודה on the אנדרוגינוס, mistakenly circumcising the wrong baby on שבת, the days a ברית may be delayed, and an incomplete מילה
overview: The גמרא finishes showing that רבי יהודה does not treat an אנדרוגינוס as a definite male in general. It proves this from an unattributed ספרא and from a משנה about the פרה אדומה waters, and explains that מילה is different because the פסוק says "כׇּל זָכָר". A new משנה then discusses a father who mixed up two babies and circumcised the wrong one on שבת. רב הונא and רב יהודה read the משנה differently, and three ברייתות report the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע in different ways. רבי אליעזר learns from עבודה זרה that any mistaken forbidden act requires a חטאת. רבי יהושע exempts someone who made the mistake while busy with a מצוה. A puzzle in רבי חייא's version is solved by asking whether שבת was actually set aside for this particular person. Next, a משנה explains why a ברית can be pushed from day 8 up to day 12, and that a sick baby waits until he is healthy, which שמואל defines as seven full days after the fever leaves. The amud ends with a משנה about leftover skin that makes a מילה incomplete, and about fixing a fleshy baby only because of מראית העין.

steps.title: An unattributed ספרא follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the ספרא teaching it just quoted counts as the view of רבי יהודה: an unattributed ספרא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And an unattributed teaching in the ספרא is the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just quoted a ספרא that does not treat an אנדרוגינוס as a definite male. Now it explains that this ספרא reflects רבי יהודה's own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that a ספרא teaching with no name attached follows רבי יהודה. So that ספרא tells us what רבי יהודה himself holds. This shows that רבי יהודה does not treat an אנדרוגינוס as a full male in every area of הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Unattributed; a teaching stated with no name attached
The ברייתא collection of halachic teachings on ויקרא (Leviticus)
A person with both male and female features

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a brand-new statement. It completes the proof from the previous lines of the גמרא by explaining whose opinion that ספרא represents.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that an unattributed ספרא follows רבי יהודה is used all over ש״ס to identify who stands behind an anonymous teaching.

phrases.english: And an unattributed teaching in the Sifra is Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: A general rule for identifying the author of an anonymous teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof begun on the previous amud by assigning the ספרא to רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה does not consider an אנדרוגינוס a definite male in every area.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An unattributed ספרא, which by rule follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Support from the משנה about sanctifying the red heifer waters
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק supports the same point from a משנה: רבי יהודה disqualifies an אנדרוגינוס, together with a woman, from mixing the ashes of the פרה אדומה into water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We also learned this in a משנה. Everyone is fit to mix the ashes into the water except a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor. רבי יהודה allows a minor but disqualifies a woman and an אנדרוגינוס. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a second proof, this time from a משנה. In that משנה, רבי יהודה groups the אנדרוגינוס with a woman and disqualifies both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the משנה ("הכל כשרים") even allows a woman, but רבי יהודה holds that only a male may do this task. He even allows a male minor, yet he still disqualifies an אנדרוגינוס together with a woman. That shows he does not count an אנדרוגינוס as a definite male, and the step ends with "שמע מינה" to lock in the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it, meaning there is support from a משנה
To sanctify, here meaning to put the ashes of the פרה אדומה into the water
A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor
Declares fit or valid
Declares unfit or invalid
Learn from this, meaning the proof stands

steps.whyThisMatters: This proof is stronger because it does not depend on the rule about an anonymous ספרא. רבי יהודה's name appears in the משנה itself.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
We too have also learned this in a mishnah:
Everyone is fit to sanctify the purification waters,
phrases.notes: This means placing the ashes of the red heifer into the water.

phrases.english: except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor.
Rabbi Yehuda deems a minor fit
and deems a woman and a hermaphrodite unfit.
phrases.notes: The hermaphrodite is grouped with the woman, not treated as a definite male.

phrases.english: Conclude from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, explicit source that supports the same conclusion as step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה does not treat an אנדרוגינוס as a definite male.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה פרה: רבי יהודה disqualifies a woman and an אנדרוגינוס from sanctifying the waters.

steps.title: Why is circumcision different?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהודה does not usually treat an אנדרוגינוס as male, the גמרא asks why he does so for מילה on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about מילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that sets up the next step. If an אנדרוגינוס is not a definite male, why does רבי יהודה allow his מילה to override שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יהודה ruled that one may break שבת to circumcise an אנדרוגינוס. That seems to treat him as a full male. The גמרא now needs to explain how this fits with the sources just brought.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is different? A formula asking why one case differs from another
Circumcision

phrases.english: And what is different about circumcision?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out a tension between steps 1–2 and רבי יהודה's ruling about מילה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יהודה counts an אנדרוגינוס as male for מילה but not for other laws.

steps.title: The verse says every male
steps.stepSummary: מילה is a special case because the פסוק says "כׇּל זָכָר". The word "כל" (every) widens the law to include an אנדרוגינוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written: "Circumcise for yourselves every male."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wording of the פסוק about מילה is broader than usual. The word "every" brings in the אנדרוגינוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אנדרוגינוס is still not a definite male in רבי יהודה's view. For מילה, though, the word "כל" includes anyone who could possibly be called male. This is a special rule for מילה, not a change in his basic status.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it is written in a פסוק
Circumcise for yourselves every male (בראשית יז:י)
Every; here it widens the law to include more people

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה does not treat an אנדרוגינוס as a definite male in general. For מילה, the word "כל זכר" includes him, so one may break שבת for his מילה.

phrases.english: Because it is written:
"Circumcise for yourselves every male."
phrases.notes: The word "every" widens the law to include a hermaphrodite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word "כל" in "כׇּל זָכָר" widens מילה to include an אנדרוגינוס, even though he is not a definite male elsewhere.

steps.title: משנה: circumcising the wrong baby on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a person had two babies, one due for מילה on שבת and one due after שבת. He forgot and circumcised the one due after שבת on שבת, so he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone had two babies, one to be circumcised after שבת and one to be circumcised on שבת. He forgot and circumcised the one meant for after שבת on שבת. He is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes a mistake: the wrong baby was circumcised on שבת, and the person is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה overrides שבת only when it is done on the eighth day. The baby due after שבת was not yet obligated in מילה, so wounding him on שבת was a forbidden מלאכה with no מצוה to permit it. Because he acted by mistake, he must bring a קרבן חטאת, even though he was busy with a real מצוה nearby.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
Babies
And he forgot
Liable; here, he must bring a קרבן חטאת

steps.confusionAlert: This 'חייב' follows רב הונא's reading of the משנה. As the גמרא reports right away (step 7), רב יהודה reads this same case as 'פטור', because in his view רבי יהושע exempts someone who erred while busy with a מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a major discussion about mistakes made while busy with a מצוה (טועה בדבר מצוה).

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ שְׁנֵי תִינוֹקוֹת,
phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who had two babies,
one to be circumcised after Shabbat
and one to be circumcised on Shabbat,
and he forgot and circumcised
the one meant for after Shabbat on Shabbat —
he is liable.
phrases.notes: He must bring a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic with a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Circumcising, on שבת, a baby who is not yet due for מילה makes one liable for a קרבן חטאת, even if done by mistake while busy with a מצוה.

steps.title: Second case: circumcising the Friday baby on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. If the father circumcised on שבת the baby whose מילה was due on ערב שבת, רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one baby was due for מילה on ערב שבת and the other on שבת, and the father forgot and circumcised the ערב שבת baby on שבת: רבי אליעזר obligates him to bring a חטאת, and רבי יהושע exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with a second mix-up case. In this case the two תנאים argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערב שבת baby's proper day was Friday, so by שבת his מילה is already late. A late מילה does not push aside שבת. That is why רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת. רבי יהושע exempts him because this baby did need a מילה, so a real מצוה was done, unlike the baby in step 5, who was not yet due at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Friday, the day before שבת
A sin-offering brought for an accidental violation of a serious prohibition
Obligates / holds him liable
Exempts

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this case up with step 5. In step 5 the wrong baby was not due yet (his day was after שבת). Here the wrong baby is overdue (his day was Friday), so he truly needed a מילה.

phrases.english: one to circumcise on Shabbat eve
and one to circumcise on Shabbat

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁכַח וּמָל אֶת שֶׁל עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בַּשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: and he forgot and circumcised the Shabbat-eve one on Shabbat
phrases.notes: That baby's eighth day was Friday, so by שבת his מילה is late.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds him liable to a sin-offering
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד לָמוּל בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וְאֶחָד לָמוּל בַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה begun in step 5 by adding a second mix-up case, which is the one under dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Circumcising the overdue ערב שבת baby on שבת by mistake: רבי אליעזר says he is liable to a חטאת, and רבי יהושע says he is exempt.

steps.title: Two versions of the משנה's first case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by reporting that רב הונא's version of the משנה's first case reads 'liable', while רב יהודה's version reads 'exempt'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב הונא teaches the משנה as saying 'liable'. רב יהודה teaches it as saying 'exempt'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a disagreement about the wording of the משנה's first case (step 5). This sets up the next step, where the גמרא gives רב הונא's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a disagreement about what the text of the משנה says, not a new halachic argument. In רב הונא's version, circumcising the 'after שבת' baby on שבת makes a person liable. In רב יהודה's version, the משנה reads 'exempt' for that same case.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that follows the משנה
Teaches / recites the text as
Liable
Exempt

phrases.english: Gemara
Rav Huna teaches: 'liable'
phrases.notes: This refers to the first case of the משנה (the baby due after שבת).

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda teaches: 'exempt'

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה (it raises the question of which version is correct)
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא מַתְנֵי ״חַיָּיב״, רַב יְהוּדָה מַתְנֵי ״פָּטוּר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to a dispute about how its first case is worded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא's version of the first case reads 'liable'; רב יהודה's version reads 'exempt'.

steps.title: רב הונא's source: no dispute in the after-שבת case
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's version is backed by a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says both תנאים agree that circumcising the 'after שבת' baby on שבת makes a person liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא teaches 'liable', as a ברייתא teaches. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע did not argue about someone with two babies, one due on שבת and one due after שבת, who forgot and circumcised the 'after שבת' baby on שבת. Both agree he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רב הונא got his version: a ברייתא that says this case is not under dispute at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, in the 'after שבת' case even רבי יהושע agrees there is liability. That baby was not yet due, so no מצוה was done at all. This fits רב הונא's version of the משנה, which reads 'liable'.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
They did not disagree
Babies

steps.confusionAlert: The text here says רבי אלעזר. In context it refers to the same תנא as רבי אליעזר of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna teaches 'liable'
as it was taught in a baraita
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yehoshua did not disagree
phrases.notes: Refers to the same תנא as רבי אליעזר of the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: עַל מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ שְׁנֵי תִינוֹקוֹת,
phrases.english: about one who had two babies
one to circumcise on Shabbat
and one to circumcise after Shabbat

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁכַח וּמָל אֶת שֶׁל אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת בַּשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: and he forgot and circumcised the after-Shabbat one on Shabbat
that he is liable

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the tannaitic source behind רב הונא's version from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's version of the משנה: 'liable' in the 'after שבת' case
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר

steps.title: Where the two תנאים really argue
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא continues: the real dispute is in the 'ערב שבת' case, where רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what did they disagree? About someone with two babies, one due on ערב שבת and one due on שבת, who forgot and circumcised the ערב שבת baby on שבת. In that case רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת, and רבי יהושע exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by naming the one case where רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע truly argue. It matches the second case of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows the argument to the overdue baby. There a real מצוה was done, just not in its proper time. So according to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, רבי יהושע exempts only when an actual מצוה was done, and that supports reading 'liable' in the first case.

keyTerms.meaning: About what did they disagree?
He forgot (an accidental mistake)
A מילה done after its proper day, which does not push aside שבת

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר (and רב הונא): for the baby not yet due, everyone agrees he is liable. For the overdue baby, רבי אליעזר says liable and רבי יהושע says exempt.

phrases.english: about what did they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: עַל מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ שְׁנֵי תִינוֹקוֹת,
phrases.english: about one who had two babies
one to circumcise on Shabbat eve
and one to circumcise on Shabbat

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁכַח וּמָל אֶת שֶׁל עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בַּשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: and he forgot and circumcised the Shabbat-eve one on Shabbat
that Rabbi Eliezer holds him liable to a sin-offering
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from step 8 by naming the case where the dispute actually exists.
steps.raayaObject: The dispute between the two תנאים is limited to the 'ערב שבת' case
steps.raayaSupportSource: Second half of the ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר

steps.title: The shared source in עבודה זרה and רבי אליעזר's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: Both תנאים learn the laws of חטאת from עבודה זרה. רבי אליעזר says that just as an accidental act of עבודה זרה requires a חטאת, so does this mistaken מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them learned this only from idolatry. רבי אליעזר holds it is like idolatry: with idolatry the Torah said 'do not do it,' and if a person does it he is liable. Here too it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע comes from. It begins with רבי אליעזר's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lays out the חטאת for accidental sins in the section about עבודה זרה. רבי אליעזר compares straight across. A forbidden act done by mistake makes you liable, so the mistaken מילה on שבת also requires a חטאת. In his view the fact that he was trying to do a מצוה does not change anything.

keyTerms.meaning: Idolatry. The Torah teaches the laws of the חטאת offering in its section.
They learned it (derived the rule)
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah / ה׳
It makes no difference; the case is the same
He is liable (here, to bring a חטאת)

phrases.english: And both of them did not derive it
phrases.notes: 'Both' means רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: except from idolatry.
phrases.notes: The Torah's section on the חטאת for an accidental sin is written about עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds: it is like idolatry,

phrases.aramaic: מָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא ״לָא תַּעֲבֵיד״,
phrases.english: just as with idolatry the Torah said 'Do not do it,'
and when one does it (by mistake), he is liable,
here too, it is no different.
phrases.notes: The mistaken מילה on שבת is also a forbidden act, so he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם לֹא לְמָדוּהָ אֶלָּא מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the argument just described in the ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, an accidental forbidden act requires a חטאת even when it was done while trying to do a מצוה, just like עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's distinction: a mistake while doing a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says the comparison to עבודה זרה breaks down. There the sin had nothing to do with a מצוה, but here the person was busy with a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע says: there, it is not a מצוה. Here, it is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהושע's side. He uses the same source as רבי אליעזר but points out a key difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who sins by mistake with עבודה זרה was not doing anything good. Here the father was trying to do the מצוה of מילה and simply mixed up the babies. For רבי יהושע, a person who makes a mistake while busy with a מצוה is exempt from a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: There (here, the case of עבודה זרה)
Here (the case of the mistaken מילה)
Where it is not a מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument comes down to one question. Does making a mistake while doing a מצוה exempt you from a חטאת? רבי אליעזר says no and רבי יהושע says yes.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua (holds):
there (idolatry), it is not a מצוה,
here, it is a מצוה.
phrases.notes: He was trying to do the מצוה of מילה, so he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: הָתָם דְּלָאו מִצְוָה הָכָא מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reasoning. It accepts the same source but separates this case from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהושע, a mistaken sin done while trying to do a מצוה does not require a חטאת.

steps.title: רב יהודה's version: the ערב שבת baby case is exempt by everyone
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reads the משנה as 'exempt'. He backs this with a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר says both תנאים agree there is no חטאת when the ערב שבת baby is circumcised on שבת by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה teaches 'exempt', as it was taught: רבי מאיר said, רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע did not argue about a person who had two babies, one to circumcise on ערב שבת and one to circumcise on שבת, and he forgot and circumcised the ערב שבת baby on שבת. Everyone agrees he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now returns to רב יהודה's version of the משנה, which reads 'exempt'. It brings a ברייתא of רבי מאיר to support it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערב שבת baby is already past his eighth day, so circumcising him is a real מצוה, just a late one. Since an actual מצוה was done, both תנאים agree there is no חטאת. This is the opposite of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ברייתא, where this exact case was the one in dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches (this is his reading of the text)
As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
They did not disagree
Friday, the day before שבת
Exempt (from a חטאת)

steps.confusionAlert: The two ברייתות flip the cases. In רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version, everyone agrees on the 'after שבת' baby and the dispute is about the ערב שבת baby. In רבי מאיר's version, everyone agrees on the ערב שבת baby and the dispute is about the 'after שבת' baby.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda teaches 'exempt,'
phrases.notes: This is his reading of the first case in the משנה.

phrases.english: as it was taught: Rabbi Meir said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua did not disagree

phrases.aramaic: עַל מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ שְׁנֵי תִינוֹקוֹת,
phrases.english: about one who had two babies,
one to be circumcised on Shabbat eve
and one to be circumcised on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁכַח וּמָל אֶת שֶׁל עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בַּשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: and he forgot and circumcised the Shabbat-eve one on Shabbat —
that he is exempt.
phrases.notes: He did a real (late) מצוה, so everyone agrees there is no חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing רב הונא's version and its reasoning, the גמרא turns to רב יהודה's competing version.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's reading of the משנה's first case as 'פטור'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי מאיר says everyone agrees on exemption in the ערב שבת case

steps.title: In רבי מאיר's version, the dispute is the 'after שבת' baby
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The real dispute is about circumcising the baby due after שבת on שבת: רבי אליעזר requires a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what did they disagree? About one who had two babies, one to circumcise after שבת and one to circumcise on שבת, and he forgot and circumcised the 'after שבת' baby on שבת. רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא of רבי מאיר finishes by naming which case the two תנאים actually argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the baby was not yet due, so no real מצוה was done at all. רבי יהושע still exempts, because the father made his mistake while busy trying to do a מצוה. רבי אליעזר holds he is liable, as in his comparison to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: About what did they disagree?
After שבת
Exempts
Obligates (him to bring) a sin-offering

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: the 'after שבת' case is liable according to everyone, and the dispute is the ערב שבת case. רב יהודה: the ערב שבת case is exempt according to everyone, and the dispute is the 'after שבת' case.

phrases.english: About what did they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: עַל מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ שְׁנֵי תִינוֹקוֹת,
phrases.english: About one who had two babies,
one to be circumcised after Shabbat
and one to be circumcised on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁכַח וּמָל אֶת שֶׁל אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת בַּשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: and he forgot and circumcised the after-Shabbat one on Shabbat —
Rabbi Eliezer obligates a sin-offering,
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts.
phrases.notes: He was busy with a מצוה when he made the mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מָה נֶחְלְקוּ עַל מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ שְׁנֵי תִינוֹקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי מאיר's ברייתא by naming the case that is actually in dispute.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's version, in which the dispute is the 'after שבת' case
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of רבי מאיר's ברייתא

steps.title: In this version too, רבי אליעזר learns from עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: Inside רב יהודה's version, the גמרא repeats that both תנאים learn from עבודה זרה. It gives רבי אליעזר's reasoning: a forbidden act done by mistake always brings a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them learned it only from עבודה זרה. רבי אליעזר holds: it is like עבודה זרה. Just as with עבודה זרה the Torah said 'do not do,' and if he does it he is liable, here too it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the dispute in רב יהודה's version, about circumcising the after-שבת baby on שבת. It uses the same reasoning it used before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are almost the same as before, but now they explain a different case. In רב יהודה's version, the argument is about the baby whose מילה was due after שבת. רבי אליעזר says the person broke a שבת prohibition by mistake, so he brings a חטאת, just like with עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not do. This is a negative commandment.
He is liable, here meaning he must bring a חטאת.
It is no different.
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם לֹא לְמָדוּהָ אֶלָּא מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: And both of them learned it only from idolatry.
Rabbi Eliezer holds: it is like idolatry,

phrases.aramaic: מָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא ״לָא תַּעֲבֵיד״,
phrases.english: just as with idolatry the Torah said 'do not do,'
and when he does it, he is liable,
here too, it is no different.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם לֹא לְמָדוּהָ אֶלָּא מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the dispute just quoted in רב יהודה's ברייתא (step 13). It repeats the wording of step 10 for this new version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: a mistaken act on שבת brings a חטאת, just like a mistaken act of עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the person was busy with a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says the comparison does not hold. With עבודה זרה the sinner was not busy with a מצוה, but here he was.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע: there, he was not busy with a מצוה. Here, he was busy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהושע's answer in רב יהודה's version. He explains why this person does not bring a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who did עבודה זרה by mistake was doing nothing good. The person here mixed up the babies because he was busy doing the מצוה of מילה. רבי יהושע holds that a person who makes a mistake while busy with a מצוה is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Busy, occupied.
There, here meaning the case of עבודה זרה.
Here, meaning the case of מילה.

steps.whatToRemember: In רב יהודה's version, the ערב שבת case brings no חטאת according to everyone. In the after-שבת case, רבי אליעזר says he is liable because it is like עבודה זרה. רבי יהושע says he is exempt because he was busy with a מצוה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua:
there, he was not busy with a מצוה;
here, he was busy with a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: הָתָם לָא טְרִיד בְּמִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אליעזר's comparison to עבודה זרה by pointing out a key difference.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע: someone who makes a mistake while busy with a מצוה is exempt from a חטאת.

steps.title: רבי חייא's report: everyone agrees he is liable in the ערב שבת case
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches a different report of רבי מאיר. In it, both תנאים agree that circumcising the ערב שבת baby on שבת by mistake makes the person liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: רבי מאיר used to say that רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע did not argue about a man who had two babies. One was to be circumcised on ערב שבת and one on שבת. He forgot and circumcised the ערב שבת baby on שבת. In that case he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third version of the dispute, from רבי חייא. This step gives the case where everyone agrees, and the next step will give the case they argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי חייא and רב יהודה say that in the ערב שבת case רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree. But in רב יהודה's version they agree he is exempt, and here they agree he is liable. So even רבי יהושע does not apply his 'busy with a מצוה' exemption to this case.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught, used to introduce a ברייתא.
They did not argue.
Liable, here meaning he must bring a חטאת.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two reports of רבי מאיר! In רב יהודה's report, both agree he is exempt in the ערב שבת case. In רבי חייא's report, both agree he is liable in that same case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya taught:
Rabbi Meir would say,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua did not disagree

phrases.aramaic: עַל מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ שְׁנֵי תִינוֹקוֹת,
phrases.english: about one who had two babies,
one to circumcise on Shabbat eve
and one to circumcise on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁכַח וּמָל אֶת שֶׁל עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בַּשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: and he forgot and circumcised the Shabbat-eve one on Shabbat,
that he is liable.
phrases.notes: Liable to bring a חטאת according to both תנאים in this version.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא: אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a different version of the same ברייתא, which disagrees with רב יהודה's report in steps 12-13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי חייא's report, circumcising the ערב שבת baby on שבת by mistake makes a person liable according to everyone.

steps.title: רבי חייא's report: they argue about the after-שבת baby
steps.stepSummary: In רבי חייא's report, the real dispute is about circumcising the after-שבת baby on שבת by mistake. רבי אליעזר says he must bring a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they argue about? A man who had two babies. One was to be circumcised after שבת and one on שבת. He forgot and circumcised the after-שבת baby on שבת. רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא of רבי חייא continues and names the case where the two תנאים argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי חייא's report, the argument is about the same case as in רב יהודה's report: the after-שבת baby. The two reports differ only in the ערב שבת case, where רבי חייא says everyone holds liable and רב יהודה says everyone holds exempt. This makes רבי יהושע exempt the case with no real מצוה but hold liable the case with a real מצוה, which seems backwards. The next step raises exactly this problem.

keyTerms.meaning: After שבת, meaning his eighth day falls on Sunday.
Obligates, makes liable.
Exempts.

steps.whatToRemember: There are three reports of the dispute. In רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ברייתא (רב הונא's source), they argue about the ערב שבת case. In רבי מאיר's ברייתא (רב יהודה's source) and in רבי חייא's report of רבי מאיר, they argue only about the after-שבת case. Those two reports differ about the ערב שבת case: רב יהודה's source says everyone exempts, and רבי חייא says everyone holds him liable.

phrases.english: About what did they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: עַל מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ שְׁנֵי תִינוֹקוֹת,
phrases.english: About one who had two babies,
one to circumcise after Shabbat
and one to circumcise on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁכַח וּמָל שֶׁל אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת בַּשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: and he forgot and circumcised the after-Shabbat one on Shabbat,
that Rabbi Eliezer deems him liable to a sin-offering
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי חייא's ברייתא by naming the case they argue about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי חייא's report, if a person circumcises the after-שבת baby on שבת by mistake, רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts.

steps.title: Why would רבי יהושע be stricter where a מצוה was done?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by רבי חייא's version. רבי יהושע exempts the person who did no מצוה, but holds liable the person who did do a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now think about it: in the second case, where he did not do a מצוה, רבי יהושע exempts him. Yet in the first case, where he did do a מצוה, he holds him liable?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking רבי חייא's version of the dispute because it seems to run backwards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, he circumcised the ערב שבת baby on שבת. That is still a real ברית, just late, so it is a מצוה, and yet everyone holds him liable. In the סיפא, he circumcised the after-שבת baby on שבת. That is too early, so it is no מצוה at all, and yet רבי יהושע exempts him. Logically, the case with the מצוה should be the easier one.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (opens a 'how can this be?' challenge)
The first clause of the teaching
The latter clause of the teaching
Exempts
Holds liable

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. 'Doing a מצוה' means circumcising a baby whose time has already come (the ערב שבת baby). Circumcising the after-שבת baby on שבת is too early, so it is no מצוה.

phrases.english: Now, Rabbi Yehoshua

phrases.aramaic: סֵיפָא דְּלָא קָא עָבֵיד מִצְוָה — פּוֹטֵר,
phrases.english: in the latter clause, where he does not perform a מצוה, exempts;
phrases.notes: Circumcising the after-שבת baby on שבת is premature, so it is no מצוה.

phrases.english: in the first clause, where he does perform a מצוה, he holds liable?!
phrases.notes: The ערב שבת baby's circumcision is valid even when late.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סֵיפָא דְּלָא קָא עָבֵיד מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal logic of רבי חייא's version from Steps 16-17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's version of רבי יהושע's position
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A case with a real מצוה should not be treated more strictly than a case with no מצוה. Yet רבי יהושע exempts the no-מצוה case and agrees to liability in the מצוה case.

steps.title: The first case is where the שבת baby was already circumcised
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ינאי explain the רישא as a special case. The person first circumcised the שבת baby early on ערב שבת, so for him שבת was never set aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי say: The first case is where he went ahead and circumcised the שבת baby on ערב שבת. So שבת was not set aside at all. In the latter case, שבת was set aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the רישא as a very specific situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture the רישא this way. He had two babies, one due on ערב שבת and one due on שבת, and he mixed them up. He circumcised the שבת baby on Friday, and then the Friday baby on שבת. Now nobody of his is left whose ברית pushes aside שבת. In the סיפא, the שבת baby was still waiting to be circumcised on שבת, so שבת was set aside for him. That is why his mistake counts as being busy with a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall of רבי ינאי
He went ahead and circumcised early
שבת was permitted to be set aside (for the ברית)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יהושע's exemption depends on a real מצוה that overrides שבת being in play at that moment. Doing a good deed in general is not enough.

phrases.english: In the school of Rabbi Yannai they say:
The first clause is where he went ahead and circumcised
the Shabbos baby on Shabbos eve,
so Shabbos was not given to be overridden.
In the latter clause, Shabbos was given to be overridden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא is an ordinary mix-up, so the case with a מצוה should be easier.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the רישא, the שבת baby was already circumcised. שבת was never set aside for this person, so his act counts as a plain mistaken מלאכה.

steps.title: But שבת is set aside for babies in general
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי objects to רב כהנא. Even in the רישא, שבת is set aside for ברית מילה for babies in general.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא: In the first case too, שבת is set aside for babies in general!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on the answer of דבי רבי ינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a ברית overrides שבת is a general rule for all eight-day-old babies. So how can we say that in the רישא שבת 'was not given to be set aside'? It seems that it was.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, editor of the תלמוד
An אמורא; here he answers רב אשי
Babies in general

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana:
In the first clause too, Shabbos was given to be overridden
with regard to babies in general!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that in the רישא 'שבת was not given to be overridden'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The permission to do a ברית on שבת is a general rule for all babies, so it applies even in the רישא.

steps.title: For this particular person, שבת was not set aside
steps.stepSummary: Babies in general do not matter here. For this man, no ברית was left that could push aside שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: For this man, at any rate, it was not given.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers that what counts is the situation of the person who did the act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether this person was busy with a מצוה that overrides שבת. He had already circumcised his שבת baby on Friday, so he personally had no ברית left that could override שבת. His act on שבת is therefore just a mistaken forbidden act, and he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: For this man
At any rate
It was not given

steps.whatToRemember: In רבי חייא's version, רבי יהושע exempts only when שבת was truly set aside for this person's ברית. If the שבת baby was already circumcised, he is liable even though he did a מצוה.

phrases.english: For this man, at any rate, it was not given.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's objection in Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the general rule and the individual's situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a ברית overrides שבת for all babies, שבת was set aside in the רישא too.
steps.terutzMaskana: What matters is whether שבת was set aside for this specific person, and here it was not.

steps.title: A baby is circumcised between day eight and day twelve
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a baby may be circumcised on day 8, 9, 10, 11, or 12, never earlier and never later.
steps.simpleTranslation: A baby is circumcised on the eighth day, or the ninth, tenth, eleventh, or twelfth day. Never earlier and never later.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the possible days for a ברית מילה, and the משנה itself will explain when each one applies (steps 23-24).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says to circumcise on the eighth day. This משנה adds that sometimes the ברית is pushed off to day 9, 10, 11, or 12. It never happens before day 8 and never after day 12, unless there is a special reason such as illness. The משנה goes on to explain each case.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A baby
Is circumcised
No earlier and no later

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A baby is circumcised at eight days,
at nine, and at ten,
and at eleven, and at twelve,
no earlier and no later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the sugya about mistaken circumcision on שבת ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ברית takes place between day 8 and day 12, never before day 8 and never after day 12.

steps.title: Why the ברית moves to day 9 or day 10
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains its own rule. A ברית is normally on day 8. A baby born during בין השמשות gets his ברית on day 9. A baby born during בין השמשות on ערב שבת gets his ברית on day 10.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? Normally a baby has his ברית at eight days. If he was born during בין השמשות, he has his ברית at nine days. If he was born during בין השמשות on ערב שבת, he has his ברית at ten days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks 'How so?' and then explains the 8 to 12 day range it just taught. This step covers day 8, day 9, and day 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בין השמשות is a ספק: it might belong to the day before or the day after. So we wait until day 8 has surely arrived, which makes the ברית day 9. When that twilight is on ערב שבת, the ברית would fall on שבת. We cannot do it then, because only a ברית that is definitely on day 8 pushes aside שבת, so it moves to Sunday, which is day 10.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (the משנה is about to explain what it just said)
in the normal way
twilight, a time that may belong to either day
he is circumcised
Friday, the day before שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Day 10 does not mean the baby is 'late' for no reason. The ברית does not happen on שבת because we are not sure that שבת is really day 8. Only a ברית that is certainly on day 8 pushes aside שבת.

phrases.english: How so?
phrases.notes: The משנה opens its own explanation of the 8 to 12 day rule.

phrases.english: In the usual way, at eight days.
phrases.notes: The basic rule from the Torah.

phrases.english: If he was born at twilight
phrases.notes: We are not sure which day he was born on.

phrases.english: he is circumcised at nine days.
phrases.notes: We wait so that day 8 has surely arrived.

phrases.english: If he was born at twilight on Shabbos eve
phrases.notes: The doubtful day 8 falls on שבת.

phrases.english: he is circumcised at ten days.
phrases.notes: A doubtful ברית cannot push aside שבת, so it moves to Sunday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 8 to 12 day range that the משנה stated in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Normal: day 8. Born during בין השמשות: day 9. Born during בין השמשות on ערב שבת: day 10.

steps.title: How the ברית can reach day 11 or day 12
steps.stepSummary: If a יום טוב comes right after that שבת, the ברית moves to day 11. If two days of ראש השנה come after it, the ברית moves to day 12.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is a יום טוב after that שבת, he has his ברית at eleven days. If there are two days of ראש השנה after it, he has his ברית at twelve days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the same case of a baby born during בין השמשות on ערב שבת. It shows how holidays right after שבת can delay the ברית even more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same rule from Step 23 applies to יום טוב. A ברית that is not surely on day 8 also cannot push aside יום טוב. Each holiday day after שבת delays the ברית by one more day, and that is how we reach day 12, the latest date in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: a Torah holiday
the New Year, which is kept for two days
right after שבת

steps.whatToRemember: Only a ברית that is certainly on day 8 pushes aside שבת or יום טוב. A doubtful case waits until after them, which is why the ברית can reach day 12 at most.

phrases.english: If there was a Festival after Shabbos
phrases.notes: Sunday is a יום טוב, so the ברית cannot be done then either.

phrases.english: he is circumcised at eleven days.
If there were two days of Rosh Hashanah after it
phrases.notes: Sunday and Monday are both holy days.

phrases.english: he is circumcised at twelve days.
phrases.notes: This is the latest day in the משנה's list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds holidays to the ערב שבת twilight case from Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יום טוב after that שבת delays the ברית to day 11. Two days of ראש השנה delay it to day 12.

steps.title: A sick baby waits until he is healthy
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds a new rule. A sick baby is not circumcised until he gets better.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sick baby: we do not circumcise him until he becomes healthy.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה teaches a separate reason to delay a ברית: the baby is sick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The day-8 rule does not override the baby's health. This delay has no limit like the 12-day list. We wait as long as it takes for the baby to recover.

keyTerms.meaning: a sick baby
we circumcise
until he becomes healthy

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical הלכה of delaying a ברית for a baby who is not well. The גמרא builds on it in the next step.

phrases.english: A sick child
we do not circumcise him until he becomes healthy.
phrases.notes: Health comes before doing the ברית on time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from delays caused by the calendar to a delay caused by sickness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sick baby is not circumcised until he recovers.

steps.title: After a fever leaves, wait a full seven days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins with שמואל. Once a baby's fever is gone, we give him seven full days to recover before the ברית.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: שמואל said: If the fever left him, we give him a full seven days to become healthy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by explaining the משנה's rule about a sick baby. שמואל explains what 'until he becomes healthy' means for a baby who had a fever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said to wait 'until he becomes healthy.' שמואל adds a rule: when the fever breaks, the baby is not yet fully healed. We wait seven full days to let him regain his strength before the ברית.

keyTerms.meaning: an early אמורא in Babylonia
the fever left him
a full seven days
to let him heal fully

steps.confusionAlert: The seven days start when the fever leaves, not when the baby was born. The ending of the fever does not count as being fully healthy yet.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practical הלכה of waiting seven days after a baby with a general sickness recovers before doing his ברית.

phrases.english: Gemara: Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: This marks the start of the גמרא on this משנה.

phrases.english: If the fever left him
phrases.notes: חמה here means fever (literally, heat).

phrases.english: we give him a full seven days to heal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what 'until he becomes healthy' from Step 25 means in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a baby's fever leaves, we wait a full seven days before the ברית.

steps.title: Must the seven recovery days be full 24-hour periods?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the seven recovery days after a fever must be counted as exact 24-hour periods.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: When we wait seven days after the baby recovers, do we need full 24-hour days, from the exact time he got better until that same time seven days later?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about שמואל's rule of seven recovery days. It wants to know how to count those days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to count. You could count seven calendar days, where a partial first day counts as a day. Or you could count seven full 24-hour periods (מעת לעת), starting from the exact hour of recovery.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the חכמים); introduces an open question
From time to time; a full 24-hour period counted from an exact hour
We require

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
Do we require from time to time (full 24-hour periods)?
phrases.notes: This refers to the seven recovery days from step 26.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מִי בָּעֵינַן מֵעֵת לְעֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to count the seven recovery days that שמואל required in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the seven recovery days must be counted as full 24-hour periods or as plain calendar days.

steps.title: Attempted proof from לודא: recovery day is like birth day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from לודא's teaching that calendar days are enough, because recovery is compared to birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what לודא taught: 'The day he gets healthy is like the day he is born.' Doesn't this mean that just as we don't need full 24-hour days when counting from birth, we also don't need full 24-hour days when counting from recovery?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching from לודא to try to answer the question. It suggests that recovery days are counted the same way as birth days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When counting eight days from birth, we use calendar days. A baby born in the afternoon can have his ברית on the morning of day 8, even though eight full 24-hour periods have not passed. If recovery day is 'like' birth day, then the seven recovery days should also be plain calendar days.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; introduces a source brought as proof
A חכם who taught this ברייתא
The day of his healing (recovery)
The day of his birth
Is it not that...? Introduces the proposed reading of a source

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Luda taught:
The day of his healing is like the day of his birth.
Is it not that:
Just as with the day of his birth
we do not require from time to time,
so too with the day of his healing
we do not require from time to time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 27 using a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the seven recovery days do not need to be full 24-hour periods.
steps.raayaSupportSource: לודא's teaching that the day of healing is like the day of birth, read as meaning both are counted the same way.

steps.title: Rejection: recovery day is stricter than birth day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: לודא's comparison does not mean the counting is the same, and recovery does need full 24-hour periods.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The day of healing is stronger than the day of birth. For the day of birth, we don't need full 24-hour periods. But for the day of healing, we do need full 24-hour periods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says recovery days have a stricter count than birth days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'like' in לודא's teaching does not have to mean 'counted exactly the same way.' The גמרא reads it so that recovery is even more demanding than birth. Counting from birth can use calendar days, but counting from recovery needs seven full 24-hour periods.

keyTerms.meaning: Is superior / stronger; here, stricter in what it requires
For whereas; sets up a contrast between two cases

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read עֲדִיף as 'easier.' Here it means the recovery count is MORE demanding: it needs full 24-hour periods, while the birth count does not.
steps.whatToRemember: Counting eight days from birth uses calendar days. Counting seven days from recovery uses full 24-hour periods (מעת לעת).
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets how long a family must wait before the ברית of a baby who was sick. The extra strictness makes sense because the baby's health and safety are at stake.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, עֲדִיף יוֹם הַבְרָאָתוֹ מִיּוֹם הִוָּלְדוֹ,
phrases.english: No, the day of his healing is superior to the day of his birth,
for whereas with the day of his birth
we do not require from time to time,
with the day of his healing
we do require from time to time.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, עֲדִיף יוֹם הַבְרָאָתוֹ מִיּוֹם הִוָּלְדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of לודא's teaching proposed in step 28.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely. לודא's comparison does not show that recovery days are counted like birth days.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'like' means 'counted the same way.' It can instead mean recovery is stricter, needing full 24-hour periods.

steps.title: New משנה: leftover skin that makes the ברית incomplete
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists the shreds of skin that, if left uncut, mean the מילה is not complete. The main one is skin covering most of the עטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are the shreds of skin that hold back the מילה from being complete: skin that covers most of the עטרה (the crown). Such a person is still treated as uncircumcised, and if he is a כהן, he may not eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It starts defining which leftover pieces of skin make a ברית count as incomplete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every leftover bit of skin matters. The key case is skin still covering most of the עטרה, which means the main part of the מילה was not done. Such a person is treated like an ערל, so a כהן in this state may not eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'; marks the start of a new משנה
Shreds or pieces of skin left over after the מילה
That hold back / make invalid until fixed
The crown (corona) of the organ
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן, which an ערל may not eat

steps.whyThisMatters: This defines when a ברית counts as done in הלכה. It matters for whether a ברית must be finished, even on שבת, and for whether a כהן may eat תרומה.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
These are the shreds
that invalidate the circumcision:
flesh that covers most of the corona,
and he does not eat terumah.
phrases.notes: A כהן with such skin left over is treated like an ערל, who may not eat תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ הֵן צִיצִין הַמְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַמִּילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic. The discussion of recovery days is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Skin covering most of the עטרה makes the מילה incomplete. Such a person is treated as uncircumcised and may not eat תרומה.

steps.title: A fleshy baby is fixed so he does not look uncircumcised
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that if a properly circumcised baby is a בעל בשר, the מוהל fixes it because of מראית העין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he was fleshy, the מוהל fixes it, because of how it looks to people.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing cases about finishing a מילה. Here the מילה is already kosher, but extra flesh makes the baby look uncircumcised, so we fix it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 was about skin that makes the מילה truly incomplete. This case is different. The מילה is already valid by law, and the only problem is how it looks. The fix is done because of מראית העין, so no one will think he was never circumcised.

keyTerms.meaning: A fleshy person. His extra flesh covers the עטרה, so he looks uncircumcised.
He fixes it, by cutting or adjusting more.
How something looks to others. Avoiding the false impression that a rule was broken.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two kinds of fixing. Shreds covering most of the עטרה make the מילה truly incomplete (Step 30). Being a בעל בשר is fixed only because of מראית העין, since the מילה is already valid.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the fleshy baby's מילה is not kosher. It is fully valid. The fix is only so he does not look uncircumcised.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two different levels of requirement. Some leftover skin makes the מילה truly incomplete, while this fix is done only so he will not look like an ערל.

phrases.english: And if he was fleshy,
phrases.notes: The מילה was done properly, but extra flesh makes him look uncircumcised.

phrases.english: he fixes it,
phrases.notes: The מוהל adjusts the flesh so the מילה is visible.

phrases.english: because of how it looks to people.
phrases.notes: The reason is appearance, not that the מילה is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from Step 30. It adds a case where the מילה is valid but still gets fixed, for appearance only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A properly circumcised baby who is fleshy and looks uncircumcised should be fixed, because of מראית העין.
